turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I'm just after your blood pressure before you go in. Left sleeve up for me.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): The left is better anyway. The right was bruised after the bloods last month, and I've been favouring it, though that's nothing to do with why I'm here.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Mm. 138 over 84, pulse 76, temperature 36.6.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): 36.6, yeah, that matches the little thermometer at home. I kept checking because my mother always said a jaw ache might be a temperature coming on.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Grand. The doctor will see you now.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, the two of you, sit in. What's brought you along today?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the jaw, doctor. When I chew there's a pain just in front of the ear, and it clicks, a little pop, and I have to stop mid-bite.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): That sounds miserable. How does it behave through the day?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Mornings are rotten, like I've been clamped shut all night. If work is mad it comes back in the evening, a sharp ache, not really a throb.
[SEG0010] person_4 (CAREGIVER): And there's grinding. I hear the teeth going most nights. He sleeps through the whole thing.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't feel it myself, but I believe him. He's not one for making things up, and some mornings the jaw is already tired before I'm even out of the bed.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is the click every time you open, or mainly when you're eating?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, mainly with food. A crust, an apple, a chop, the right side clicks, and for a second the mouth won't open the full way, then it gives.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever with this, or have you felt unwell in yourself?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): The stress has been desperate. We've a new accounts package and I'm on the laptop till half nine, and the face tightens when I'm staring at the screen.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll come back to the stress. On the fever, though, any temperature, or feeling hot and shivery?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No fever at all. I haven't felt hot once.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long has the jaw been at you?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Err. Last winter, or the one before. I couldn't put a date on it. It just crept in.
[SEG0020] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He only said it out loud when the clicking got loud at dinner. Before that he'd just go quiet over the food.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): What eases it, if anything at all?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): A warm cloth helps a small bit, and the soup days are grand. Paracetamol takes the edge off, but I don't like swallowing it every single day.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): What regular medicines are you taking?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Metformine for the sugar, 500 milligrams twice a day, for years now. And Mizartan for the pressure, 40 milligrams every morning.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything else from the chemist?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Omprazole, 20 mg, once a day before breakfast, for the acid. I never miss that one, because the heartburn is rotten if I do.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the evening Metformine, does that actually get taken?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, not always. If I'm home late I forget it, maybe two or three evenings a week.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Are the teeth themselves sore, or is it the joint?

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): The teeth are fine, the dentist went over them and found no holes. I had a crown put on a back tooth years ago after it cracked on a mint, but that side is quiet now. It's the joint that clicks, not the tooth.
[SEG0031] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He rubs the right side of the jaw in the car. I see it at the lights, every time the traffic stops.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the stress, you feel that makes the pain worse?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, definitely. A deadline and that evening the pain is sharper and the click is louder. A quiet Saturday it's only a niggle, unless I chew a steak.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does the jaw ever lock and stay shut? Any swelling, or a bad taste?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No locking that stays. No swelling I've seen. And no bad taste, I was watching for that in case a tooth was going off.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): How is the sleep, apart from the grinding he hears?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Of. I wake once or twice and roll over. It's not a proper insomnia.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke at all, or take a drink in the evenings?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I gave up the cigarettes eight years ago. A glass of wine at the weekend, and not through the week.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): What are you doing for work these days?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm an accounts clerk, screens all day. I jam the phone between the ear and the shoulder, which is probably stupid for this jaw.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me feel the joint and have a look in the mouth, if you're alright with that.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand, it's the right one, just there. Go easy though, it gets very tender if it's pressed.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tender over the right jaw joint as you open, and I can feel the click. No swelling. Teeth look fine, and the throat is clear.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, that's the exact spot. It hops a little toward the ear, not down into the neck at all.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): I think this is the jaw joint itself, a temporomandibular problem, with the grinding and the stress feeding it. I don't think it's an infection.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): That's a relief. My uncle had a jaw infection after a tooth came out, and I had myself half convinced, even with the dentist saying the teeth were sound.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Soft food for a couple of weeks, nothing chewy or crusty. And get a boil-and-bite mouth guard from the chemist for the night.
[SEG0049] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll stand over him until he wears it. He'll say it's uncomfortable after one night, I know him.

[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I will wear it, I promise, even though I hate plastic in the mouth. I'll do the soups and the scrambled egg and leave the crusts, and I'll keep a note of the bad evenings the way I do with the sugar readings.

[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Paracetamol is grand when you need it, up to one gram four times in the day, with a bit of food. No chewing gum. If it's not easing in three weeks, come back and we'll think about the dental hospital. If it locks solid before that, ring us.

traps.happens: The transcript looks like speech-to-text: drug names are sometimes spelled wrongly ('Omprazole', 'Mizartan' for telmisartan, 'Metformine'), fragments and fillers appear ('Err', 'Of.', 'Mm.', 'Umm'), numbers are sometimes digits and sometimes words.
traps.label_rule: Medicine names are recorded as written in the transcript (name) with a normalized/generic name ONLY when the true drug is certain from context (a drug 'for the pressure' written 'Mizartan' is NOT certain enough: leave generic_name empty). Fragments and fillers are never facts.
